programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Fiù ’s nuair a tha thu den bheachd gur e fuamhaire a th’annad, bu choir cuimhneachadh gu bheil e furasta tuiteam is thu fhèin a fhliuchadh ma tha glumagan mòra ann Even when you think you’re a giant, you should remember that it is easy to fall and get wet if the puddles are large enough.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Flop ag ullachadh stuth builgeanan is tha e a sealltainn dha Bing agus Pando mar a bhios iad a sèideadh is a dèanamh builgeanan. Chaneil Bing toilichte nuair a chì e Pando gam bruthadh ach, aig a cheann thall, tha e ag ionnsachadh gu bheil e spòrsail. Flop prepares a bubble mixture and shows Bing and Pando how to blow bubbles. Bing isn’t happy when Pando bursts them, but he soon learns that it is fun to do so.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha thìd ann airson facal Abadas ùr agus turas 'aba-do-be-dee' ùr cuideachd! An-diugh, 's e 'bior-deighe' am facal. Tha na h-Abadas ag ionnsachadh gu bheil ceangal aige ri uisge, ach càite an lorg iad e agus cò bu chòir a dhol ga lorg? It is time for a new Abada word and a new 'aba-do-be-dee' adventure. This time the word is 'icicle'. The Abadas learn that it has something to do with water, but where will they find it and who should go on the adventure?

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Air latha brèagha earraich, tha bèibidhean aig Blor! Tha Àtaidh agus Tilidh ag ionnsachadh mun t-saothair a tha an lùib a bhith a’ coimhead às dèidh bèibidhean a tha a’ fàs. On a beautiful springtime day, it looks like Bop's had little babies! Abney and Teal find out just how much trouble growing babies can be.

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha Peicein is Lòra ag argamaid mu dheidhinn cò aca a bu chòir na riaghailtean a dhèanamh suas airson geama Ghriogair is Raghnaill. Fhad ’s a tha iadsan a’ feuchainn ri obrachadh a-mach cò aca a bu chòir a bhith nan sgiobair, tha Griogair agus Raghnall a’ cumail a’ cluich às aonais a’ bhuill. Petit and Laura argue about who should be the one that makes the rules of Greg and Roman's game. While they decide who should be the captain, Greg and Roman wait for them to make a decision and continue playing without the ball.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Ramsay MacMahon a’ leughadh Seall an rud a th’ agamsa. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Anthony Browne agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Jo NicDhòmhnaill. A bedtime story for young children. Ramsay MacMahon reads Seall an rud a th’ agamsa, written by Anthony Browne and translated into Gaelic by Jo Macdonald.

programme.title: The Deep/An Doimhne
programme.desc: Tha creutair mì-àbhaisteach anns an uisge – a’ coiseachd air grunnd na mara agus a’ tarraing buaireadh. Dè idir a th’ ann? Feumar a stad – ach ciamar? There’s an unusual creature in the water, walking across the ocean floor and causing havoc. What on earth is it? It must be stopped, but how?

programme.title: Na Speuran
programme.desc: Thèid air turas suas dha na speuran cuide ris an Speuradair Bekah! Air an turas fànais iongantach seo tha i ag innse dhuinn mu Bhoireannaich ann am Fànas agus mun obair chudromach a tha iad air a dhèanamh. Bidh i cuideachd a’ toirt sùil air teothachd san fhànais. Blast off into space with Astronaut Bekah! In this amazing space voyage, she tells us about the valuable work of women in space. She also takes a look at temperature in the cosmos.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha caraid shònraichte aig Pòl…’s e creutair a th’ innte à fànas. Tha i car coltach ri bruis toidhleit. Dave gets a girlfriend… who turns out to be an alien. One that looks a little bit like a familiar household item…

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Anna ag ullachadh airson deuchainn nam baidhseagal aig an sgoil agus tha i glè mhath air. Chan eil Pòl leth cho math rithe, ach le baidhseagal ùr bho phàrantan, tha e an dòchas gum faigh e tron deuchainn. Gu mì-fhortanach, chan eil am baidhseagal ùr aige buileach ag obair mar as còir agus tha e ag adhbharachadh trioblaidean do Phòl. Ach a dh’aindeoin sin, ’s dòcha gum buannaich e rudeigin air a shàilleabh… Anna is practising for the school cycling test and is rather good at it. Dave however isn’t quite as skilled, but with a new bike from his parents he really hopes to pass. Sadly, this new bike doesn’t play fair and Dave has some trouble, but maybe he might just end up being the best at something…

programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra
programme.desc: Mairi Rodgers explores The Alnwick Garden in Northumberland. Tha Màiri Rodgers a’ gabhail cuairt tro Ghàrradh Alnwick ann an Northumberland.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Singer and Gaelic teacher Margaret Macleod Nicholson is Joy’s studio guest, and Calum Maclean visits Scotland’s newest city and once ancient capital, Dunfermline.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Fuine
programme.desc: In Skye, Calina MacDonald makes her favourite recipe - a ginger and marmalade slice. Reasabaidhean gràdhach agus cruthachaidhean ùra bho Ghriogair MacLeòid agus caraidean.

programme.title: Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean/Wild Senses
programme.desc: Rannsachadh air na dòighean annasach a tha fradharc bheathaichean air leasachadh. An exploration of the strange evolution of animal vision.

programme.title: Brunch le Abigail
programme.desc: Airson treat sgoinneil airson brunch, tha Abigail a’ dèanamh Smoothie le Deit is Teòclaid. Tha e math ’s tha e math dhut, agus e air a stobhadh le maitheas an t-samhraidh. For a splendid brunch treat, Abigail makes a date and chocolate smoothie. It's wholesome and tasty, as well as being packed with summer goodness. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: Air sgàth mar a tha trioblaidean slàinte air a bhith aig Ruairidh agus a chridhe a’ fàiligeadh, feumaidh e a bhith mothachail mu na tha e ag ithe. Tha Ùisdean air aontachadh taic a thoirt dhà agus tha iad a’ cruthachadh reasabaidhean far a bheilear a’ seachnadh salann is siùcar, ach aig a’ cheann thall – chan eil ionndrainn orra! Tha reasabaidhean airson Giomach le Sabhs Jerk, Anann air a Ghriligeadh le Sabhs Ruma Charamail, Bonnach-èisg Criospach agus Tart Bakewell Dearcan is Àmoin uile air an atharrachadh gus biadh blasta is fallain a chruthachadh do Ruairidh. Part of Roddy’s health scare with heart failure means he has to adjust what he eats. Uisdean has agreed to help him out as they come up with some recipes where neither salt nor sugar is used, and in the end neither ingredient is missed! Lobster in jerk sauce, grilled pineapple with rum caramel sauce, crispy fishcake and berry almond Bakewell tart recipes are all tweaked to provide Roddy with tasty and healthy meals. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Iorram – Boat Song
programme.desc: Alastair Cole takes a cinematic journey into the past and present of the Outer Hebrides, mixing voices, stories and songs from the 20th century with images of island life today.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: From Ice to Fire: The Incredible Science of Temperature
programme.desc: Everything around us - from the tiniest insect on Earth to the most distant stars of the cosmos - exists somewhere on a vast scale from cold to hot. In this series, physicist Dr Helen Czerski explores the extraordinary science of temperature. She unlocks the extremes of the temperature scale, from absolute zero to searing heat of stars - and reveals how temperature works, how deep its influence on our lives is, and why it's the hidden force that has shaped our planet and the entire universe. In episode one, Helen ventures to the bottom of the temperature scale, revealing how cold has shaped the world around us and why frozen doesn't mean what you might think. She meets the scientists pushing temperature to the very limits of cold, where the normal laws of physics break down and a new world of scientific possibility begins. The extraordinary behaviour of matter at temperatures close to absolute zero is driving the advance of technology, from superconductors to quantum computing.

programme.title: The Ruth Ellis Files: A Very British Crime Story
programme.desc: Series re-examining the Ruth Ellis case. In part two, Gillian turns her attention to Ruth's trial, which took just a day and a half. Her lawyer pursued a risky defence strategy.

programme.title: Personal Cinema: Maggie Smith
programme.desc: In a programme first broadcast in 1970, Maggie Smith talks to Michael Aspel about her career and chooses scenes from some of her favourite films, including Way Out West, The Last Hurrah, On the Waterfront, Some Like It Hot and The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie.

programme.title: Tea with Mussolini
programme.desc: Florence 1935. A circle of English ladies settled in the cultured city take an orphan boy, Luca, under their wing. But even a propaganda encounter with Il Duce cannot protect them when war comes, and it falls to Luca and two brash American women they barely tolerate to ease their existence. Semi-autobiographical drama from Franco Zeffirelli.

programme.title: How to Get Ahead
programme.desc: Stephen Smith explores the flamboyant Baroque court of the Sun King, Louis XIV. Louis created the Palace of Versailles so he could surround himself with aristocrats, artists, interior designers, gardeners, wigmakers, chefs and musicians. Hordes of ambitious courtiers scrambled to get close to the king, but unseemly goings-on in the royal bedchamber reflected the quickest path to power.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate why a bank suddenly refused to let one couple re-mortgage because of the way their home had been constructed – despite approving the mortgage five years earlier. Experts share advice on how to secure a mortgage even when things go wrong with your property. Also on the programme, has an updated booking system made it easier for Muslims hoping to attend the Hajj pilgrimage? And at the advice clinic in Mansfield, the team help a woman being hounded for payments for a phone contract that isn’t hers.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion struggles to find fault with a mid-terrace in Stoke, but could there be any hidden nasties? Another terrace in Staffordshire requires more attention! And a flat in south east London has Jacqui fretting over the short lease.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion heads to an antiques fair in the town of Llandeilo in West Wales, where experts Philip Serrell and Charles Hanson help the red and blue teams as they compete to see who can buy the three most profitable items to take to auction. Christina also gets hands-on with the ancient art of silversmithing at a family business in the heart of nearby town Laugharne.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Rav and Nick listen in to calls by a scammer posing as Sky’s broadband department as he tries to steal money from UK victims believing he is fixing their internet connection. As the team try to contact a woman in the process of being defrauded, they face a previously unseen foe – a fire alarm in the scam hub. Will the unusual interruption prevent them from saving the woman from the scammer’s clutches?

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Having been to the Lake District over 50 times, today’s couple have decided to stop visiting and start living in one of the UK’s most spectacular national parks. The about-to-be-retired couple need Steve Brown’s help to find them, and their two rescue cats, a new forever home in the Cumbrian countryside.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Kevin, Dave, Alan and Ken – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Kevin, Dave, Alan and Ken – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate why a bank suddenly refused to let one couple re-mortgage because of the way their home had been constructed – despite approving the mortgage five years earlier. Experts share advice on how to secure a mortgage even when things go wrong with your property. Also on the programme, has an updated booking system made it easier for Muslims hoping to attend the Hajj pilgrimage? And at the advice clinic in Mansfield, the team help a woman being hounded for payments for a phone contract that isn’t hers.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion struggles to find fault with a mid-terrace in Stoke, but could there be any hidden nasties? Another terrace in Staffordshire requires more attention! And a flat in south east London has Jacqui fretting over the short lease.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion heads to an antiques fair in the town of Llandeilo in West Wales, where experts Philip Serrell and Charles Hanson help the red and blue teams as they compete to see who can buy the three most profitable items to take to auction. Christina also gets hands-on with the ancient art of silversmithing at a family business in the heart of nearby town Laugharne.

programme.title: BBC News at One

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Rav and Nick listen in to calls by a scammer posing as Sky’s broadband department as he tries to steal money from UK victims believing he is fixing their internet connection. As the team try to contact a woman in the process of being defrauded, they face a previously unseen foe – a fire alarm in the scam hub. Will the unusual interruption prevent them from saving the woman from the scammer’s clutches?

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Television and radio presenter Angellica Bell and her husband, former fellow children’s TV favourite Michael Underwood, team up with Nicki Chapman to find a family home in the Devon countryside. The property-savvy pair might even roll up their sleeves and get mucky, as there are talks of full-scale renovations at a 1930s period property.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Having been to the Lake District over 50 times, today’s couple have decided to stop visiting and start living in one of the UK’s most spectacular national parks. The about-to-be-retired couple need Steve Brown’s help to find them, and their two rescue cats, a new forever home in the Cumbrian countryside.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Dom and Lucia help an iconic Glasgow landmark that has lost its lustre, save an endangered Chinese unicorn, and discover how street art is changing one city before our very eyes.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Kevin, Dave, Alan and Ken – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: Wild Cameramen at Work
programme.desc: Some of the world's rarest and most dangerous animals live on dry land. Capturing them on film requires great patience and specialist skills. In this episode, Gordon Buchanan and Mark Smith reveal how the wildlife-tracking skills they learned back home in Scotland have allowed them to film some of the natural world's most intimate moments, including being the first to film wild pandas mating and snow leopards hunting.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: It's time for some early summer colour as Carole Baxter makes the first of her visits to classic Scottish gardens. She visits Glenarn, which has a fabulous collection of rhododendrons looking their best right now. Back at Beechgrove Garden, George Anderson and Calum Clunie are busy refreshing the grass and gravel plot and planting new varieties. Calum demonstrates how to take cuttings from a fuchsia, and there are some ideas on how to manage your plot if you are unlucky enough to have club root in your vegetable patch. And there are all the usual handy hints.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: As spring turns to summer, Dougie is in Cairngorms National Park to find out how authorities are protecting precious habitats from the risk of wildfires. Cammy is on his Ayrshire farm at the peak of lambing season, and Anne ventures to the Isle of May to find out how extreme weather is driving apart one species of birds that mate for life. She also reflects on her own special family connection to the island and pays a visit to the lighthouse where her grandfather was posted. Elsewhere, journalist Rachel Bell follows in the footsteps of the Highland Lady who left her stylish mark in Braemar.

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: Police in Inverness raid a flat and discover a laboratory containing a number of dangerous chemicals and electrical circuitry. They evacuate the area and call in the bomb disposal team. PC Stephen Cooper co-ordinates a desperate search for two missing hillwalkers in Glencoe, and in the Cairngorms, cops investigate a suspected shotgun attack on the nest of a protected bird of prey.

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: Gary McAllister made the game of football look easy. The proverbial classy midfield player who saw the full picture, and could affect it, in the crucial seconds before his opponent. Unprepared to succumb to a story that began with knock-backs, Gary wrote his own place in the history and folklore of every club he played for - a winner at Motherwell, champion at Leeds, immortal at Liverpool, and a Scotland captain of some repute. But there were lows to counter the highs, and Gary discusses these with searing honesty. However, he is not defined by the hard times, but rather the moments where his class and will to win elevated him to the very top of the game. With contributions from Steven Gerrard, Gordon Strachan and Ardal O’Hanlon, this is the story of one of the greatest Scotland players of his, or any, generation.

programme.title: Stevens & McCarthy
programme.desc: Awkward husbands make for an awkward chat, and a man-spreader learns a lesson.

programme.title: Scotcast
programme.desc: Conversation about Scotland’s biggest news stories, hosted by Martin Geissler.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: Traffic officers McKirdy and Singh fall out over issuing a ticket to a family member but make up over some music at the end of their shift. City cops McLaren and Fletcher meet a familiar face while attending a bag snatch, and rural officers Mackay and McIntosh deal with some quarrelsome landowners. Call Centre Operator Maggie LeBeau has some useful advice for homebuyers, Sergeant Karen Ann Millar has to deal with a curry pie and a birthday cake, and Volunteer Officer Beattie finds himself following the leads of five dogs. The Chief explains the importance of listening to the public and the implausibility of some people's names, before heading to London for a press conference to launch a combined Scottish Police Force/London City Force initiative with an old colleague.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: It’s the first day of sixth form, and Mike is looking forward to a bit of social mobility. He thinks he’s way better than the group of so-called 'loser' friends he’s somehow accrued, and aspires to higher things. But for now, he’s stuck with powergeek Sonny and Dan, a lad who only communicates in put-downs, and he’s going to find it hard to shake them off: Mike, Sonny and Dan all take the mobility bus to school. Mike has cerebral palsy, Sonny uses a wheelchair, and Dan ‘Syndrome’ Simmons has Down’s Syndrome. So Mike, Sonny and Dan are trapped together – at least for the ride to school.

programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: In northern Asia, life defies hostile extremes. In Russia's Lake Baikal, a seal pup must take evasive action when its ice den starts to melt. Hokkaido's thermal springs are a haven for dancing red-crowned cranes. On the Tibetan Plateau, a lone Himalayan wolf hunts antelope. Fish owls thrive in the forests where Russia and China meet. On the Kamchatka Peninsula, brown bears hunt salmon to prepare for hibernation. Elsewhere in Japan, bats hibernate beneath snow, while red foxes and sea eagles compete for food. In Arctic Russia, polar bears wait on isolated lands for the return of sea ice.

programme.title: Freddie Flintoff's Field of Dreams
programme.desc: A world away from their lives in Lancashire, sporting legend Freddie Flintoff is determined to give his unlikely cricket team of teenagers a trip they will never forget and teach them important life lessons for when they return to the UK. But whilst preparing the boys for their toughest cricket match so far, the reality of living together pushes Freddie to his limits.

programme.title: The Traitors India
programme.desc: The palace is abuzz with tension as the players prepare for a mission that forces them to pair up. All duos face the same choices - benefits for themselves or a heavy increment to the prize pot. Trust shatters and true colours are revealed as they throw each other under the bus. Back in the palace, the players bear the brunt of their choices. The atmosphere turns volatile with heated arguments and new suspicions. At Circle of Shaq, new players face accusations, and the game takes an unexpected turn when the Traitors are handed an explosive secret mission. One wrong move could change the game forever. As truths and lies collide, the stakes have never been higher.

programme.title: The Traitors India
programme.desc: The morning begins with a chilling announcement that leaves the players stunned - someone’s fate hangs in the balance after the events of the previous night. As the group retrace their steps, whispers of suspicion and fear ripple through. The mission takes on an ominous tone as the players work together to uncover who has been murdered, with eerie clues leading them closer to the truth. With emotions running high and survival on everyone’s mind, the group is left shattered to its core. Back at the palace, as the players try to navigate the web of lies, a shocking revelation forces everyone to reconsider their strategies and question everything they thought they knew about the game.

programme.desc: Garden experts Diarmuid and Carol are joined by guest judge and passionate gardener Patrick Grant to continue the search to find Northern Ireland’s greatest garden. The first garden they view is a coastal sanctuary, and owner Heather’s pride and joy in Millisle. Heading inland to Benvarden, Ballymoney, retired dairy farmer Shaun has created Brockagh Wood, a 15-acre woodland and wildlife garden in memory of his wife. Finally, they visit Iona Cottage in Greyabbey, home to Darren and Victoria, with its herbaceous borders and cut flower garden. Diarmuid, Carol and Patrick are searching for a garden which the owner has poured their heart and soul into creating. Which will they decide is worthy of a place in the Greatest Garden final?

programme.title: MasterChef
programme.desc: Heat 3 is upon us, which means one thing: six exciting new amateur cooks have left their home kitchens ready to compete for one of four coveted MasterChef aprons.

programme.title: LS Lowry: The Unheard Tapes
programme.desc: The story of the 'matchstick man' painter, one of Britain’s most beloved artists, revealed as never before through intimate and previously unheard hidden recordings. Recorded by a young fan, Angela Barratt, in 1972, the tapes uncover much about Lowry's life story and the changing north he captured in his iconic paintings. The voices in this film are real, lip-synced by actors Ian McKellen and Annabel Smith.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: The competition ramps up as the celebrity trio, TV icon Anneka Rice, comedian Shane Todd and Radio 1Xtra DJ Remi Burgz, return for day two of the quiz. Vernon Kay keeps control as host, while unreliable guide Paul Gorton leads a tour of Cardiff. Momentum is building as the countdown to the weekly final begins.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Bristol-based Diana and her daughter Millie are dreaming of a fresh start in the sunny Somerset countryside, with enough land for a little flower farm to bloom. Alistair Appleton is on hand to help them sow the seeds of their new life. Along the way, he meets a couple who have swapped cider apples for grape vines, planting their very own vineyard in the heart of this amazing county.

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway adventure in Uzbekistan continues in Samarkand, one of the oldest cities in Central Asia. Michael discovers the national passion for bread, which leads him to a family bakery where he learns how to bake special, bagel-like loaves. The great conqueror Tamerlane made Samarkand his capital in the 14th century, and at his tomb, Michael learns of the brutality and military prowess of the man who is today Uzbekistan’s national hero. The region’s global prominence grew out of the silk trade, with silk carpets being the ultimate luxury. Michael learns how secret codes are woven into traditional patterns and appreciates the skill that makes these carpets sell for tens of thousands of pounds.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Set against the dramatic backdrop of the Malvern Hills, Gardeners’ World comes from the spectacular RHS Malvern Spring Festival in Worcestershire. Rachel de Thame and Joe Swift share everything the show has to offer. Gardens, plants and expert advice, as well as tips and tricks to try at home – no matter the amount of outdoor space. There’s a visit to the Devon-Somerset border to meet a grower who, with the help of a couple of feathered friends, has transformed a woodland landscape into a stunning nursery for the humble hosta. After a drastic career change to follow her dream, one designer explains why she is using her first show to demonstrate the art of pressing flowers. There’s also a time travel visit back to the 1970s for a houseplant fanatic who’s taken her inspiration from her grandmother’s house. It’s a spring celebration not to be missed!

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents the fourth heat of this series of the classic quiz where contenders take on the famous black chair under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are Detectorists, the ‘Alice’ books of Lewis Carroll, British politics in the 1960s and Sir Elton John.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be alright!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The team visit Chepstow to help a multigenerational family of four create a beautiful home. They have to clean up after a menagerie of pets, create storage solutions and modernise the family dining room.

programme.title: Super Smart Animals
programme.desc: For centuries, the idea of intelligent animals struck most people as ridiculous. But not any more - the latest science reveals that animals are a lot smarter than we thought. From skateboarding dogs to chimp maths geniuses, Liz Bonnin embarks on a worldwide search for the planet's most intelligent animals, devising some ingenious IQ puzzles and even putting herself to the test to find out. Liz gets creative with dolphins, shares a eureka moment with orangutans and defends the reputation of the human race when she goes head-to-head with a chimp genius in a test of maths and memory. There is an octopus escapologist, John Humphrys puts a goldfish through its paces on Mastermind, and Tillman the skateboarding dog wows crowds in Los Angeles. Prepare to be amazed, entertained and even outwitted by the world's Super Smart Animals.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel invites members of the public to bring along their antiques for examination. In the gardens of Knightshayes Court in Devon, the team of experts uncover a copy of a play with royalty on the cast list and a suite of jewellery which was probably worn at the court of Napoleon. Plus some fabulous Doulton vases and an incredibly rare 17th-century jewellery box.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin and his team of experts invite members of the public to bring their antiques to be viewed and valued, with an option to sell at auction.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Deirdre O'Kane, Jay Rayner, Tessa Sanderson and Iwan Thomas take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway tour through Uzbekistan continues in the lush oasis surrounding the historic city of Samarkand. Here, he uncovers the Central Asian origins of the apple, a fruit that travelled to Europe along the Silk Road. Exploring vast orchards, he witnesses how millions of apples are grown and processed here each year. Boarding a high-speed train along the old Trans-Caspian Railway, Michael hears how the Russians toiled to build this remarkable line through the shifting sands of Uzbekistan’s steppe. In Bukhara, he explores the faded magnificence of an abandoned Russian imperial palace. He then enters the city’s Islamic heart, and standing in the shadow of the Ark, the city's striking fortified citadel, he unearths the deadly intrigue between Britain and Russia in what became known as the Great Game - and discovers the fate of two British officers thrown into the infamous 'bug pit'.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Emma suspects the pond is being visited by more than their local fishermen after secret cameras reveal a variety of hungry callers. The Williamsons take their ram lambs to a prestigious sale on the mainland, hoping to make big money and secure their reputation as top tup breeders. Lucy and Lottie enter the young handlers competition at the Arran Show.

programme.title: MasterChef
programme.desc: A brand new batch of amateur cooks enter the MasterChef kitchen, ready to compete in the first round and take their shot at culinary stardom.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: The RNLI respond to over 9,000 shouts each year - and what often gets people into trouble in the first place are the hidden dangers. In Porthcawl, on the south west coast of Wales, the crew receive a call about a swimmer who’s been swept out to sea in a rip current - as his wife and son watch on helplessly from the beach. On the Cornish coast, the Sennen Cove and Penlee crews respond to reports of a 31,000-ton cargo ship that’s about to run aground on the Wolf Rock lighthouse, ten miles from Land’s End. On the east coast of Scotland, the strong offshore winds at North Berwick cause the crew to be called out to two shouts in quick succession. And on the Thames, the Chiswick crew race to the rescue of a party boat that has lost engine power - and is now drifting dangerously upriver.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul, Bob and trusty terrier Ted travel to Blakeney Point in North Norfolk for a sea-fishing adventure. Blakeney Point is a four-mile spit of shingle and sand beach bank, with the North Sea on one side and the Glaven Estuary on the other. It is a nature reserve and an important nesting ground for terns and gulls. There is also the chance they may spot a seal in the sea. After a day of mixed fortunes, they take a boat back to the car and head to their accommodation for the evening: Bear’s Cottage, which was built in 1856 and is surrounded by 200 acres of trees, including giant redwoods and noble firs.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O'Connell.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc: Surgeons face a difficult dilemma in the middle of a life-saving bile duct cancer operation. A chest sarcoma proves more challenging than expected, with no room for error.

programme.title: This Is a Bomb: The Nevada Casino Heist
programme.desc: Meticulous and methodical, Big John engineers his ransom scheme with military precision. On paper, it’s flawless. But as the deadline approaches, nothing goes according to plan, and two battles unfold simultaneously: a high-stakes ransom exchange and a desperate race to stop a bomb designed to be unstoppable. Precision planning meets a chaotic reality, and one miscalculation on either side could mean catastrophe.

programme.desc: Bristol-based Diana and her daughter Millie are dreaming of a fresh start in the sunny Somerset countryside, with enough land for a little flower farm to bloom. programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway adventure in Uzbekistan continues in Samarkand, one of the oldest cities in Central Asia. Michael discovers the national passion for bread, which leads him to a family bakery where he learns how to bake special, bagel-like loaves. The great conqueror Tamerlane made Samarkand his capital in the 14th century, and at his tomb, Michael learns of the brutality and military prowess of the man who is today Uzbekistan’s national hero. The region’s global prominence grew out of the silk trade, with silk carpets being the ultimate luxury. Michael learns how secret codes are woven into traditional patterns and appreciates the skill that makes these carpets sell for tens of thousands of pounds.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Set against the dramatic backdrop of the Malvern Hills, Gardeners’ World comes from the spectacular RHS Malvern Spring Festival in Worcestershire. Rachel de Thame and Joe Swift share everything the show has to offer. Gardens, plants and expert advice, as well as tips and tricks to try at home – no matter the amount of outdoor space. There’s a visit to the Devon-Somerset border to meet a grower who, with the help of a couple of feathered friends, has transformed a woodland landscape into a stunning nursery for the humble hosta. After a drastic career change to follow her dream, one designer explains why she is using her first show to demonstrate the art of pressing flowers. There’s also a time travel visit back to the 1970s for a houseplant fanatic who’s taken her inspiration from her grandmother’s house. It’s a spring celebration not to be missed!

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents the fourth heat of this series of the classic quiz where contenders take on the famous black chair under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are Detectorists, the ‘Alice’ books of Lewis Carroll, British politics in the 1960s and Sir Elton John.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be alright!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The team visit Chepstow to help a multigenerational family of four create a beautiful home. They have to clean up after a menagerie of pets, create storage solutions and modernise the family dining room.

programme.title: Super Smart Animals
programme.desc: For centuries, the idea of intelligent animals struck most people as ridiculous. But not any more - the latest science reveals that animals are a lot smarter than we thought. From skateboarding dogs to chimp maths geniuses, Liz Bonnin embarks on a worldwide search for the planet's most intelligent animals, devising some ingenious IQ puzzles and even putting herself to the test to find out. Liz gets creative with dolphins, shares a eureka moment with orangutans and defends the reputation of the human race when she goes head-to-head with a chimp genius in a test of maths and memory. There is an octopus escapologist, John Humphrys puts a goldfish through its paces on Mastermind, and Tillman the skateboarding dog wows crowds in Los Angeles. Prepare to be amazed, entertained and even outwitted by the world's Super Smart Animals.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel invites members of the public to bring along their antiques for examination. In the gardens of Knightshayes Court in Devon, the team of experts uncover a copy of a play with royalty on the cast list and a suite of jewellery which was probably worn at the court of Napoleon. Plus some fabulous Doulton vases and an incredibly rare 17th-century jewellery box.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin and his team of experts invite members of the public to bring their antiques to be viewed and valued, with an option to sell at auction.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Deirdre O'Kane, Jay Rayner, Tessa Sanderson and Iwan Thomas take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway tour through Uzbekistan continues in the lush oasis surrounding the historic city of Samarkand. Here, he uncovers the Central Asian origins of the apple, a fruit that travelled to Europe along the Silk Road. Exploring vast orchards, he witnesses how millions of apples are grown and processed here each year. Boarding a high-speed train along the old Trans-Caspian Railway, Michael hears how the Russians toiled to build this remarkable line through the shifting sands of Uzbekistan’s steppe. In Bukhara, he explores the faded magnificence of an abandoned Russian imperial palace. He then enters the city’s Islamic heart, and standing in the shadow of the Ark, the city's striking fortified citadel, he unearths the deadly intrigue between Britain and Russia in what became known as the Great Game - and discovers the fate of two British officers thrown into the infamous 'bug pit'.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Emma suspects the pond is being visited by more than their local fishermen after secret cameras reveal a variety of hungry callers. The Williamsons take their ram lambs to a prestigious sale on the mainland, hoping to make big money and secure their reputation as top tup breeders. Lucy and Lottie enter the young handlers competition at the Arran Show.

programme.title: Scrum V
programme.desc: Lauren Salter and guests preview the weekend's rugby action, including Wales women's final Six Nations match against Italy in Cardiff.

programme.title: Nigella: At My Table
programme.desc: Nigella cooks more warming, comforting and inspirational recipes. Perfect for winding down at the end of a long day, there's a cosy supper of chicken with red grapes and marsala, followed by a deeply divine sunken chocolate amaretto cake with crumbled amaretti cream dolloped alongside. For a dish that's as simple to make as it is rewarding to eat, there's Nigella's mussels with pasta, and just as delicious is her autumnal radicchio, chestnut and blue cheese salad. Her egg tortilla pie with a crisp crust, soft yolked eggs, salty ham and melted cheese is a pleasure to behold.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul, Bob and trusty terrier Ted travel to Blakeney Point in North Norfolk for a sea-fishing adventure. Blakeney Point is a four-mile spit of shingle and sand beach bank, with the North Sea on one side and the Glaven Estuary on the other. It is a nature reserve and an important nesting ground for terns and gulls. There is also the chance they may spot a seal in the sea. After a day of mixed fortunes, they take a boat back to the car and head to their accommodation for the evening: Bear’s Cottage, which was built in 1856 and is surrounded by 200 acres of trees, including giant redwoods and noble firs.

programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be alright!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The team visit Chepstow to help a multigenerational family of four create a beautiful home. They have to clean up after a menagerie of pets, create storage solutions and modernise the family dining room.

programme.title: Super Smart Animals
programme.desc: For centuries, the idea of intelligent animals struck most people as ridiculous. But not any more - the latest science reveals that animals are a lot smarter than we thought. From skateboarding dogs to chimp maths geniuses, Liz Bonnin embarks on a worldwide search for the planet's most intelligent animals, devising some ingenious IQ puzzles and even putting herself to the test to find out. Liz gets creative with dolphins, shares a eureka moment with orangutans and defends the reputation of the human race when she goes head-to-head with a chimp genius in a test of maths and memory. There is an octopus escapologist, John Humphrys puts a goldfish through its paces on Mastermind, and Tillman the skateboarding dog wows crowds in Los Angeles. Prepare to be amazed, entertained and even outwitted by the world's Super Smart Animals.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel invites members of the public to bring along their antiques for examination. In the gardens of Knightshayes Court in Devon, the team of experts uncover a copy of a play with royalty on the cast list and a suite of jewellery which was probably worn at the court of Napoleon. Plus some fabulous Doulton vases and an incredibly rare 17th-century jewellery box.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin and his team of experts invite members of the public to bring their antiques to be viewed and valued, with an option to sell at auction.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Deirdre O'Kane, Jay Rayner, Tessa Sanderson and Iwan Thomas take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway tour through Uzbekistan continues in the lush oasis surrounding the historic city of Samarkand. Here, he uncovers the Central Asian origins of the apple, a fruit that travelled to Europe along the Silk Road. Exploring vast orchards, he witnesses how millions of apples are grown and processed here each year. Boarding a high-speed train along the old Trans-Caspian Railway, Michael hears how the Russians toiled to build this remarkable line through the shifting sands of Uzbekistan’s steppe. In Bukhara, he explores the faded magnificence of an abandoned Russian imperial palace. He then enters the city’s Islamic heart, and standing in the shadow of the Ark, the city's striking fortified citadel, he unearths the deadly intrigue between Britain and Russia in what became known as the Great Game - and discovers the fate of two British officers thrown into the infamous 'bug pit'.

programme.title: Scrum V
programme.desc: Lauren Salter and guests preview the weekend's rugby action, including Wales women's final Six Nations match against Italy in Cardiff.

programme.title: Nigella: At My Table
programme.desc: Nigella cooks more warming, comforting and inspirational recipes. Perfect for winding down at the end of a long day, there's a cosy supper of chicken with red grapes and marsala, followed by a deeply divine sunken chocolate amaretto cake with crumbled amaretti cream dolloped alongside. For a dish that's as simple to make as it is rewarding to eat, there's Nigella's mussels with pasta, and just as delicious is her autumnal radicchio, chestnut and blue cheese salad. Her egg tortilla pie with a crisp crust, soft yolked eggs, salty ham and melted cheese is a pleasure to behold.

programme.title: MasterChef
programme.desc: A brand new batch of amateur cooks enter the MasterChef kitchen, ready to compete in the first round and take their shot at culinary stardom.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: The RNLI respond to over 9,000 shouts each year - and what often gets people into trouble in the first place are the hidden dangers. In Porthcawl, on the south west coast of Wales, the crew receive a call about a swimmer who’s been swept out to sea in a rip current - as his wife and son watch on helplessly from the beach. On the Cornish coast, the Sennen Cove and Penlee crews respond to reports of a 31,000-ton cargo ship that’s about to run aground on the Wolf Rock lighthouse, ten miles from Land’s End. On the east coast of Scotland, the strong offshore winds at North Berwick cause the crew to be called out to two shouts in quick succession. And on the Thames, the Chiswick crew race to the rescue of a party boat that has lost engine power - and is now drifting dangerously upriver.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul, Bob and trusty terrier Ted travel to Blakeney Point in North Norfolk for a sea-fishing adventure. Blakeney Point is a four-mile spit of shingle and sand beach bank, with the North Sea on one side and the Glaven Estuary on the other. It is a nature reserve and an important nesting ground for terns and gulls. There is also the chance they may spot a seal in the sea. After a day of mixed fortunes, they take a boat back to the car and head to their accommodation for the evening: Bear’s Cottage, which was built in 1856 and is surrounded by 200 acres of trees, including giant redwoods and noble firs.

programme.title: This Is a Bomb: The Nevada Casino Heist
programme.desc: Meticulous and methodical, Big John engineers his ransom scheme with military precision. On paper, it’s flawless. But as the deadline approaches, nothing goes according to plan, and two battles unfold simultaneously: a high-stakes ransom exchange and a desperate race to stop a bomb designed to be unstoppable. Precision planning meets a chaotic reality, and one miscalculation on either side could mean catastrophe.

programme.desc: Duggee thought his tie was a little bit plain, so he added some accessories and now it looks amazing. The Squirrels admire Duggee’s new look and want to learn how to accessorise themselves. The first step for the Squirrels is to find something they’d like to change. The Squirrels each bring a different item - wellies, a T-shirt, headband, helmet and… a potato. They grab sequins, patches, feathers and lights, and then showcase what they have all done. Norrie has added sequins to her T-shirt and made it into a new wonderfully sparkly outfit. Betty has added loads of useful items to her headband, like a calculator and a pencil, to wear it on all occasions. Roly has painted glow-in-the-dark paint on his wellies, and now he can splash in the dark. Tag has painted his helmet and added horns so he looks super-turbo! Roly has turned his potato into a beautifully made-up face with pink and yellow hair. The Squirrels want to accessorise everything. Soon enough, the whole of the Clubhouse and the town are new and improved, but the Squirrels are getting tired. There’s a chance they may have got carried away, so they go to work toning it down a touch. Less is more!

programme.desc: Bella and Lift enjoy making funny honk noises with tubes! Together, they set off to explore the floors of Playtime Towers. In the Sing Song Forest, Tincy finds some terrific tubes in her web that are perfect for making music in Tincy’s Tubey Band. Kingsley and Queenie have fun in the Fortress of Fun by playing a game of ‘Big Bunny, Little Bunny’. In Boxtropolis, Sketch makes fearsome Tubey Dragons with the Playtimers - hear them roar!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing and Sula find a helium balloon stuck in a tree in the park. They both want to play with it at the same time, so Flop makes two strings and they invent a noisy balloon game called stuck duckies. When they run in opposite directions, the balloon flies away, and Flop volunteers to be the stuck duckie so the game doesn't have to end.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘pumpkin’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. There is an orange pumpkin, a bumpy pumpkin and a pumpkin with lots of seeds. The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Dermot is upset when he misses a goal and struggles to express himself.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Lou wakes up to find himself on a lily pad in the middle of the lake. He freaks out at first, but his Calm Inner Voice comes to the rescue.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: After finding some pasta, the Froglets create a rock band with maracas, a drum and a saxophone.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are in a back garden where they see a grandad dozing in a deckchair, covered by a newspaper. The Twirlywoos watch as his grandson comes out and covers a patio table with a tablecloth. When the young man goes back inside, the Twirlywoos take the tablecloth and decide to use it to cover other things in the garden - a potted plant, a bird bath. The grandson comes back with a tea tray and is surprised to find the tablecloth missing, but each time he replaces it, the Twirlywoos take it again. Finally they end up covering the old man and the grandson is very surprised to find his grandad wearing the tablecloth like a cartoon ghost! Peekaboo comes out of his house covered in mysterious spots. He shakes himself and the spots fly up into the air. When the Twirlywoos return the spots drift down and cover Toodloo. She spins around and manages to get rid of them, only to find that they are now covering Great BigHoo! He shakes himself to get rid of the spots but they land on Chickedy and Chick. They find that they can blow the spots away and all the Twirlywoos band together to blow the spots out of the boat.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin meets Kayson to spend the day outdoors, and they make sure they've got everything they need for the weather before George joins them for a delicious ice cream. Mr Tumble is trying to dry his washing despite the weather. There's forecast fun in the spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words hat, rainbow and ice cream.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po enjoy a game of musical statues. It takes the Teletubbies a few turns to work out that when the music stops they must stand very still.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome babies Layla, George, Isobel, Lincoln, Jason, Willow and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are different types of Paper, which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding safe, baby appropriate paper inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun song ‘Colourful Paper’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children look for imaginary monkeys, learn British Sign Language signs for monkey, tree and crocodile, then sing and sign Five Little Monkeys.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Spring is the time of year when lots of different plants grow. Abbie and James join Aaron in the garden for a fun game of big plant, small plant, taking it in turns to spot plants of different sizes. They soon find a tiny one that has just poked its head above the soil - but where has it come from?

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: It’s the day of the annual Teddy Bear Party. Murphi is making sandwiches, and Rebecca has made jelly. A little mishap inspires Murphi’s first monster make – a tiny toadstool pot. The Mini Monsters create paper cup critter puppets, and Rebecca’s cousin, Fiona, calls to share her idea for a cupcake case flower. Murphi’s mega monster make is a teddy bear box, helped by some round boxes brought along by the Recycling Express.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: When Ginger gets a nasty tummy ache, the Pea-Rexes have to find a special soothing herb.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: When it’s Bingo’s turn to bring her kindergarten’s Bob Bilby puppet home and record their weekend in the scrapbook, the family resolve to put down their screens and show him a good time.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are out walking around in the rain with Duggee and notice a rainbow! But before they know it, it’s gone and the Squirrels are devastated. They decide to make their own rainbow and go off in search of all the colours from everything around them, including strawberries, carrots and bananas. Duggee shows the Squirrels what he has been working on too - a rainbow cake!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Do you know someone who is having a first day sometime soon? Everything will be OK!

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers go on a special autumn walk that starts in the daytime and finishes in the dark, where they all get to drink hot chocolate. On the way, they discover where a beaver has been at work, play inside a tree, make shadows with their lanterns and even fly like bats!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Eden and Ava make their very own necklaces using colourful beads. Eden kindly makes one for her best friend and gives it to her as a surprise. Later, the sisters go rollerskating in the park. It’s Ava’s first time skating on her own, but luckily Eden has lots of good tips for her. Will Ava be able to keep up with her big sister and become a super skater?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Mateo’s mum is from Chile and she has shown him how to make a special Chilean dish. Sopaipillas are made with sweet potato dough and served with a colourful pebre made from tomatoes, spring onions and coriander. Mateo decorates his table with lots of plants and colourful flowers. There are even a few alpacas and llamas joining the party! Mateo also shows off his dancing skills to his friends while wearing a traditional Chilean costume. Let’s hope all of Mateo’s friends like the taste of his food.

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In today's episode, Maddie is visiting a supermarket, where she finds out what barcodes are and how they work. At the checkout, we learn how an infrared scanner reads barcodes to find out what items we are buying and how much they cost. Maddie uses a special camera to see how the right items in the stock room get to the right shelves in the supermarket. Next, Maddie heads to a factory to see how fishcakes are made. We see how fresh cod is filleted and added to other ingredients on a massive scale. Maddie uses a special camera to show how the ingredients are shaped and go under a breadcrumb shower to come out as a fishcake.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Diesel is a hearing dog for his teenage owner, Rayane, who is deaf. This means he doesn’t hear everything. Diesel is trained to listen out for important sounds that Rayane might miss. Diesel is Rayane’s ears. Together, they’re unstoppable! Diesel wakes up wondering where he is. Then, he remembers – he’s on a camping trip with Rayane and his friends Grace and Karim. And Mum’s come too! Rayane’s even made a dreamcatcher from sticks and leaves he found around the campsite. But now it’s time to go home, so there’s lots they need to do. After a breakfast of boiled eggs and toast, Diesel helps Rayane brush his teeth. It’s Diesel’s job to filter out all the other sounds at the campsite and let Rayane know when the timer goes off to let him know he’s brushed for long enough. Then, while the humans pack up camp, making sure not to leave any litter behind, Diesel has to listen out for Dad’s text so they can all meet him at the car park. The campers excitedly carry their kit back to meet Dad. But Rayane has left his dreamcatcher behind! Can Diesel follow the trail of familiar sounds to help Rayane find the campsite again – and collect Rayane’s missing dreamcatcher?

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet two tapirs, Inca and Mani - a mother and her son. These incredible animals are almost like three animals in one, with a body resembling a pig, the feet of a rhino and the nose of an elephant. Next, they head into the dark to encounter another animal that loves fruit: the fruit bat, or flying fox. Hanging upside down, the flying foxes feed nearby, giving Aneeshwar and Lizzie the chance to meet these furry-faced bats. Finally, Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover the wild connection between these two remarkable animals.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: The Brooklyn-Bells are on holiday with Gramps, so Waffle is staying at Angela’s dog kennels for a couple of nights. During a face-to-face call with Waffle, the Brooklyn-Bells check their wonder dog is settling in and ensure he has his favourite snuggly toy with him, PegStar. Angela tries to settle Waffle but he whines, he’s missing his Brooklyn-Bell family and looks at their photo on the wall of his kennel. Angela resorts to calling the Brooklyn-Bells and explains that when dogs are very disruptive, she expects their owners, or someone they know, to pick them up. Jess has an idea – there’s someone who might be able to pick Waffle up in the morning - Mrs Hobbs!

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Baba and Oona experience snow – for the very first time!

programme.title: Small Potatoes
programme.desc: Animated series about a group of singing potatoes. In this swinging homage to the Sinatra era, the Small Potatoes sing about how they are no average spuds.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Yukee and TapTap spend the night in a tent and are surprised to meet some beautiful, musical fireflies!

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: While helping Mum sort through some of the postcards on the fridge, Maddie and Triggs imagine themselves travelling all over the world with their very cool uncle.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Norrie skips into the Clubhouse and greets her friends. Together, they reflect on their first meeting. Arriving with her parents in a long limousine, Norrie, her parents and her 72 siblings flood out of the car. It's just Norrie who is going to stay at the Clubhouse, though, and enjoy some well-needed quiet. She can play alone and hear herself think! But after a while, she misses the hustle and bustle, so Duggee introduces Norrie to Enid the cat. Together, they venture into the Clubhouse, and Norrie has a friend so she isn't alone, but she still has a little bit more room than she would have at home!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Four is the new block on the block and he can't wait to share how much he loves to be square! Learn all about the number four with Numberblock Four.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: When Alphablock E opens his smoothie bar, he discovers that he has run out of fruit to make the drinks. He asks, 'who can help?'. A friendly parrot replies with a speech bubble: 'I CAN'. E learns to read this, and the parrot leads him into the forest. The parrot finds Alphablock O and Alphablock S - HE CAN and SHE CAN help. They give E oranges and strawberries, but he needs more fruit. The parrot leads him to a grove full of fruit trees. Who can help E pick the fruit? When more Alphablocks appear, E learns to read the final speech bubble: 'WE CAN'. Soon, he has smoothies for everyone.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: It’s showtime! Justin and his friends put on a play, whilst Mr Tumble has a go at making a puppet theatre. But managing all his actors proves harder than he thought.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po are trying very hard not to make any noise. Then they make as much noise as possible during the Tubby Phone Dance.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers discover how sunflowers play an important role in the environment. They find out that they are made up of lots of tiny nectar-filled flowers, which attract pollinators like bees and butterflies. They also learn that they can be homes for insects like ladybirds, who protect them from other insects that like to munch on sunflowers. On the way, they enjoy some sunflower seed snacks and pretend to be sunflowers following the sun!

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: It’s the Den’s summer fete, and Jaz is excited to do a chicken and egg mascot dance with her dad, but soon realises she’s double-booked herself and might not have time to do both.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this episode, Grace shows off three amazing machines that help with farming! Grace drives a massive compost turner, shows off a machine that makes hay bales and then picks some tasty carrots in a carrot harvester!

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: It's pea crumble for lunch at Pup School, and when Biscuit gets peas stuck in her fur, Dodge mishears and thinks she has fleas. The misunderstanding sends the rest of the pups into a frenzy, thinking that fleas are spreading around the school. When Dodge takes a moment to double-check the facts, everything becomes clear.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Eden and Ava pretend to be superheroes and go on a mission to rescue their toy!

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: Animated series. When Mr McGregor fills a bird table with sunflower seeds, Squirrel Nutkin becomes dangerously obsessed with raiding it.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: As Roly makes his usual noise in the Clubhouse, Duggee and the Squirrels reminisce about how completely different Roly was when he first arrived. Hiding behind his dad, Roly wasn't loud at all but impossibly quiet! As Duggee shows Roly around the Clubhouse, he squeals, hides and hangs off his dad, and just seems altogether too shy to fit in. Duggee has a great idea to introduce Roly to Norrie, thinking a friend will help him to settle in. But Roly is still too shy, so Duggee and Norrie start doing things with him, knowing this will help him to embrace the fun of the Clubhouse. While painting, playing with balloons and yelling, Roly begins to truly find his voice and be himself! Soon, Roly hardly noticed if his dad was around at all.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Sunny is writing a book about his favourite vet, but first he needs to ask her questions. Vida lets Sunny tag along on a day of house calls, so she can tell him everything he wants to know – in song!

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Chilli decides to become a superhero called Super Chilli! His superhero skills are put to the test when Evil Pea covers Supertato in sticky honey, but Chilli’s heat saves the day.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The eagle family are performing synchronised flight. The ducklings are blown away and join the eagle family, who teach them how to fly in formation. Weasy feels left out and finds a way to fly 'for real' so that he can also take part.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Preston is in costume as everyone’s favourite character, Dewey Dragon, but he isn't ready for how demanding Dewey’s fans are. Mojo and Bo need to help him escape the crowd.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and Bingo enlist their giant invisible friend to show Mum and Dad who’s boss.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: The shadow of a monster causes panic among the Piris, apart from Nugget, who is keen to investigate a new mystery. She finally tracks down the creature, but is all exactly as it seems?

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: In a game of hairdressers, Bingo has to find her voice, while Bluey has to find her ears.

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: Dr Ollie forgets who he asked to take the role of the wizard in his play! Ava’s memory-jogging machine helps him recall, but things get confusing at the nursery.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: While Zoe helps Doug with his homework project about Alaska, Simon and Jess take Waffle and Evie to the shops to buy new school shoes. But Waffle's attempts to help end up causing chaos.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi is busy making a half birthday card for baby Oscar, but with ukulele practice, library reading and Teacup the dog to play with, she has a lot to do. She wishes for more versions of herself, and four colourful Rafis appear. Chaos ensues, until Dash encourages Rafi to take charge. She gets each Rafi to focus on one job - crafts, reading, music and play. At the café, the Rafis sing for Oscar, present the card, and then merge back into one.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: When JoJo can’t find her favourite Captain Chloe storybook, Gran Gran suggests they make up their own story. As they create their pirate quest, JoJo learns that when you make up your own story, you get to decide what happens next.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Scarf Lady's jukebox inspires a knitted instrument band.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Nothing is going right for any of the Clangers today. Mother’s new plant is drooping, Tiny’s new tune doesn’t sound very good, Granny’s knitting colours clash, Major’s rocket has broken down and Small’s night light has run out of glow honey. But suddenly a wave of beautiful coloured light from a strange star passes over the planet and has a magical effect - everything changes for the better. All the Clangers are delighted until they notice that the star is fading away before their very eyes.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa chase a butterfly, and MeMo is gentle when it lands on their hand. At the Play Tree, they play with a bubble blower. MeMo blows a big bubble, but BaBa forgets to be gentle and pops it. The Yummies and MeMo teach BaBa to be gentle when petting Yummy Dog and handling some ripe strawberries. On the Lullaby Lake, BaBa is very gentle when the butterfly returns to settle on their hand.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: In a magical forest, colourful characters have adventures and are read stories. Makka Pakka takes a ride on the Ninky Nonk. The Tombliboos are playing inside their house when the Ninky Nonk stops outside. They decide to join Makka Pakka on the Ninky Nonk, but it leaves without them. The Tombliboos take a ride on the Pinky Ponk to help them catch the Ninky Nonk.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Kate Winslet tells the story of a unicorn whose search for inspiration leaves him with a bad case of the grumps.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s Banana revealing yet another astonishing secret about herself in the opera piece, I’ve Got a Secret.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: As Bing gets ready to go to Sula's house, he feels sneezy and hot, so Flop decides that Bing needs to stay at home and keep his germs to himself. Even though Bing is soon tucked up on the sofa with a hot honey and lemon drink, he's very disappointed that he can't play with Sula. But Sula and Amma bring him a carroty bagel to wish him a speedy recovery.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: When the Tubby Phone rings, Dipsy comes slowly down on the Dup Dup to answer it - and then goes back up again! The Teletubbies all have fun doing the Dipsy Tubby Phone dance and watch a Tummy Tale about a boy travelling up in a lift that takes him into the treetops.

programme.title: Tee and Mo
programme.desc: Preschool animation about a baby monkey and his mother. Mo is excited about her new bed and can't wait to try it out. However, she's not the only one.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Evil Pea cheats Chilli out of winning floofy teddies at a funfair made from sweets, so Supertato and the Veggies must get the teddies back before it’s too late!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: It's Bing's third birthday! Bing shows Sula, Pando and Coco how to do the waka-oke. But when Pando doesn't do it properly, a frustrated Bing hides under his blankey. Flop gently helps Bing to understand that Pando likes to do things differently to him. They celebrate Bing's birthday under his blankey, before Amma, Coco and Charlie bring in pass-the-parcel.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Mojo needs to deliver a pizza to a very hard-to-reach island, but some stubborn seabirds have their eye on the pizza. Will Mojo have to go supersonic to get past them?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Ready for another day at Squirrel Club? Find out what happens to the chickens in space, whether anyone can be an artist, and if Duggee will ever find the Squirrels playing hide-and-seek.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee thought his tie was a little bit plain, so he added some accessories and now it looks amazing. The Squirrels admire Duggee’s new look and want to learn how to accessorise themselves. The first step for the Squirrels is to find something they’d like to change. The Squirrels each bring a different item - wellies, a T-shirt, headband, helmet and… a potato. They grab sequins, patches, feathers and lights, and then showcase what they have all done. Norrie has added sequins to her T-shirt and made it into a new wonderfully sparkly outfit. Betty has added loads of useful items to her headband, like a calculator and a pencil, to wear it on all occasions. Roly has painted glow-in-the-dark paint on his wellies, and now he can splash in the dark. Tag has painted his helmet and added horns so he looks super-turbo! Roly has turned his potato into a beautifully made-up face with pink and yellow hair. The Squirrels want to accessorise everything. Soon enough, the whole of the Clubhouse and the town are new and improved, but the Squirrels are getting tired. There’s a chance they may have got carried away, so they go to work toning it down a touch. Less is more!

programme.desc: Bluey and Bingo enlist their giant invisible friend to show Mum and Dad who’s boss.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: In a game of hairdressers, Bingo has to find her voice, while Bluey has to find her ears.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: When Grandmaster Glitch builds his effigy in ice, his digging threatens the Lambert Glacier in Antarctica.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Peter, Benjamin and Lily are tempted by a mysterious hoard of radishes, Lily finds herself caught in Mr Tod's trap. Can Peter find a way to rescue Lily before Mr Tod reaches her?

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. Kwazii finds a mysterious, unbreakable coconut, so the Octonauts seek out the help of some large, island-dwelling coconut crabs to open it.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: When an alien ship crashes in Numberland, the Numberblocks decide to help the alien get back home. The alien can create lots of blocks like the Numberblocks, so they build a tower into the sky.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The Alphablocks meet a metal box that goes beep, and soon it's walking and talking and wishing it could be like its new friends. This episode introduces the '-ee-' digraph and the words beep, see, seed, feet, feel and weep.
